_comment: MOBILE_UI.md §23 (2026-10-21): the order of the @ suggestions (the composer, the canvas and the page editors), the same on every client. recent: who spoke recently, from the messages held locally. Each list is oldest first (thread: the thread's parent and replies; channel: the loaded timeline); a message counts unless deleted or of type system; only the newest `cap` counting messages of each list (default recent_messages); the thread's senders first, newest first, then the channel's, each id once. rank: filtering as before (a username starting with the query or a display name containing it, case-insensitive; not deactivated; a bot only when it is an AI bot). People sorted by match (a non-empty query: a username or display name starting with it before one only containing it), then tier (0 recent, in that order; 1 members of the conversation, a DM's participants; 2 everybody else; 3 me, even when recent), then the display name (collation for ja), then the username (code points). Then the groups (by name) and @channel / @here as before. expected: usernames (groups and channel / here by name), at most `limit`. users: ai = an AI bot (role bot, bot_kind ai); bot = another bot (role bot); deactivated = deactivated.

recent.name: channel: newest first, each once, no deleted or system messages
thread: its senders first (the parent included), then the channel's
cap: only the newest counting messages of each list

cases.name: empty query: recent speakers (not me), members, everybody else, me; then the groups and @channel / @here
the limit cuts the same order
no context: by display name, me last
a prefix match before a substring-only one, even a recent speaker; me last among the prefix matches
within a match quality: recent, then members, then everybody else
a display name starting with the query is a prefix match (case-insensitive)
username and display-name prefixes alike, by display name; no plain bot, no deactivated user
the groups and @channel after the people
